question: The use of animal-derived ingredients in medicines is common, yet EU residents often cannot identify these components due to inconsistent or unclear labelling practices. For ethical, religious, medical or dietary reasons many patients require transparency in order to make informed choices. Given that EU consumer legislation already provides for clear labelling in other sectors, improved disclosure in medicinal products would strengthen patient rights and trust while imposing minimal burden on industry. 1.

In the light of the issues faced by millions of consumers, can the Commission indicate whether it intends to propose legislation requiring mandatory and standardised labelling on packaging and patient information leaflets of all animal-derived ingredients used in medicinal products?
Additionally, can the Commission state whether it will consider establishing a centralised, publicly accessible database listing such ingredients for authorised medicines marketed in the EU?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.11.2026) The current EU pharmaceutical legislation, as well as the new EU general pharmaceutical legislation1, provides that the origin of the excipients needs to be declared in the product information where this is required for the safe and effective use of the medicinal product.

During the marketing authorisation procedure, excipients of human or animal origin are subject to specific assessment, and applicants must provide the competent authorities with the relevant information on the quality, safety and control of such materials and, where relevant, on their origin.

Whilst the mandatory labelling on packaging and patient information leaflets of all animalderived ingredients is not required, all assessment reports including information related to the human and animal origin of the excipients, are available on the website of the European Medicines Agency for medicines authorised centrally, or on the websites of national competent authorities for medicines authorised nationally.
This information helps patients and healthcare professionals choose the appropriate medicinal product.
1 COM/2023/193 final and COM/2023/192 final. The publication in the OJ is expected early December 2026,
with an entry into force 20 days after the publication in the OJ.
